extracted.intended_audience: Prospective Fulbright U.S. Student Program applicants (U.S. citizens and At-Large applicants)
extracted.subtask_short: applying to Fulbright U.S. Student Program
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step official guidance for preparing and submitting an application to the Fulbright U.S. Student Program, including eligibility, application pathways (through institution or At-Large), deadlines, and award-type selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current U.S. Student eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: United States citizens who are currently enrolled in undergraduate or graduate degree programs are eligible to apply. If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you will apply through that institution, even if you are not currently a resident there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find the Fulbright Program Adviser on your campus.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Citizen (not a student) eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen, will hold a bachelor’s degree by the award start date, and do not have a Ph.D. degree, then you are eligible to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-enrolled applicants should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying. Candidates with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. The Getting Started page will provide information on eligibility and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artist eligibility / Creative & Performing Arts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright U.S. Student Program welcomes applications in the creative and performing arts. Arts candidates for the U.S. Student Program should have relatively limited professional experience in the fields (typically 7 years or less) in which they are applying.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Artists with more experience should consider applying for the Fulbright Scholar Program. Creative & Performing Arts projects fall under the Study/Research grant category and are available in all countries where Study/Research grants are offered. Arts applicants should consult the Creative & Performing Arts Fields of Study section for information about available fields and supplementary materials requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Professor/Administrator guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a U.S. citizen and a professor or administrator at a U.S. institution and are interested in applying for a Fulbright Scholar Award, you will need to apply through fulbrightscholars.org.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To support your students in applying for a U.S. Student Program award, please connect with the Fulbright Program Adviser at your institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. Citizen applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are a non-U.S. citizen interested in applying for a Fulbright Award to the United States, you will need to apply through the Fulbright Commission or U.S. Embassy in your home country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find out more information on the Fulbright Visiting Scholar Program or Fulbright Foreign Student Program.

rubrics_metrics.name: National deadline and application finality
rubrics_metrics.description: The national deadline is Tuesday October 6, 2026 at 5 pm Eastern Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason. Please carefully review application proof for accuracy prior to submission. You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your Fulbright Program Adviser cannot do this on your behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine applicant type (institution vs At-Large)
rubrics_metrics.description: You will apply either through a U.S. institution or At-Large. If you are currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program at a U.S. college or university, you are strongly encouraged to apply through that institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are not currently enrolled, you may apply through your most recent U.S.-based institution that has a Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA), provided that the institution is willing and able to accommodate alumni applications. All other candidates will apply as At-Large applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus application procedure and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fulbright Program Adviser (FPA) will set a campus application deadline for the institution’s students, which is typically 4-6 weeks earlier than the final October deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All candidates applying through a U.S. institution must complete the Fulbright application through the Fulbright online application system by the campus deadline; all supporting materials as outlined in the Application Components section, must also be included by the campus deadline date. You will mark your application ‘Ready for Campus Review’ once it is complete and it will lock your application for the duration of the campus review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus review, interview, and revision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your application has been completed and marked ready for institutional review, the Fulbright Program Adviser will schedule a campus interview for you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Following the interview and before the national deadline in October, you may have the opportunity to revise your application based on feedback provided by the Fulbright Program Adviser and the campus review committee. Your FPA will unlock your application after the campus review is complete. You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your Fulbright Program Adviser cannot do this on your behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant responsibility for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible for submitting your own application before the National Deadline; your Fulbright Program Adviser cannot do this on your behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason. Please carefully review application proof for accuracy prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: At-Large application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: At-Large candidates must submit their applications through the Fulbright online application system by the national deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Candidates are responsible for ensuring that all supporting documents are attached to the online application, as outlined in the Application Components. Application submissions are final. Applications cannot be unsubmitted for any reason. Please carefully review application proof for accuracy prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select award type
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 3: Select Award Type — Study/Research Awards, English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards, Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study/Research Awards: Offered for projects in all Academic and Creative & Performing Arts fields. Applicants can propose their own independent study/research projects, or, in some countries, can propose to enroll in a graduate program. Arts applicants should follow Creative & Performing Arts guidance. English Teaching Assistant (ETA) Awards: Places grantees in educational centers overseas to supplement local English language instruction and to provide a fluent speaker presence in the classrooms — see the English Teaching Assistant Award section for country availability. Fulbright-Fogarty Fellowships in Public Health: Offered through a partnership with Fogarty International Center; designed for candidates currently enrolled in medical school or in a graduate-level program interested in global health. The basic requirements and process for applying for the Fulbright-Fogarty Program are the same as for any Fulbright U.S. Student Study/Research Grant — see that section for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use available resources to pick correct award
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for Picking the Correct Award include Tutorial Videos and Webinars, and Award Search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tutorial Videos and Webinars can assist you in learning more about each award type. Award Search allows you to narrow down opportunities by educational background, grant type, and world area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review country opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Select country(ies) of interest and review available awards and eligibility requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Step 4: Review Country Opportunities to determine which awards and fields are offered in each country and any country-specific eligibility or requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review application components
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult the Application Components section for required materials and any field- or award-specific supplementary materials (e.g., Creative & Performing Arts supplementary materials). Ensure all supporting documents listed there are prepared and attached by the applicable deadline (campus or national).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application open period
rubrics_metrics.description: The application is open annually from early April to mid-October.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the Competition Timeline for this cycle dates. Applicants applying through an institution will prepare a completed application by their campus deadlines, prior to the national deadline. Contact the Fulbright Program Adviser at your institution for more information.
